description: O11 (REFACTOR over STATIC ENTITY RECORDS): repoint, delete and duplicate on top of what job:static-entity-lifecycle left written - the ContactStatus (was Status) with the records Open (was Active), Closed (was Inactive) and Pending, and the two real consumers of Open: the DefaultValue of Contact.StatusId and the filter of Contact_CountActive, both saying Entities.ContactStatus.Open. Nothing is born here before the duplicate, on purpose. WHAT THIS JOB PINS DOWN, measured: (A) the replace of one IRecord by another IRecord of the same entity repoints the TWO consumers by key (consumers 2, rewired 2, stillPointingAtFrom 0, consumersOfTo 2) and the platform regenerates the text: the default becomes Entities.ContactStatus.Pending and the filter 'Contact.StatusId = Entities.ContactStatus.Pending'; the usages of Open falls from 2 to 0 and that of Pending rises from 0 to 2, with the same two consumer keys. (B) after the replace the delete of Open passes WITHOUT force (brokenConsumers 0) and Records goes down from 3 to 2; the same delete before the replace is refused naming the two consumers (tests/jobs-negative/delete-static-record-in-use.json). (C) the duplicate of a static entity is the Ctrl+D of the Studio: ContactStatus2 is born in the same parent, with the 3 attributes, the 2 records and the values copied, the Description copied word by word, its own GetContactStatus2 and its own type 'ContactStatus2 Identifier' - and WITHOUT author consumers: the only consumer that the usages finds for it (count 1, real 1) is the IAttribute of the 'ContactStatus2 Record', the anonymous structure that the PLATFORM generates with any entity. (D) because of that generated consumer, the delete of the copy without force is refused with "delete: refused, IStaticEntity 'ContactStatus2' is used by 1 consumer(s): IAnonymousStructure:ContactStatus2 Record/IAttribute:ContactStatus2" (measured): it is the ONLY force of this job, and it serves to break a consumer that no author wrote. The delete returns brokenConsumers 1 and the find of ContactStatus2 afterwards still returns that IAttribute - the anonymous record of the copy is left behind in the module, with a clean Verify. (E) what does NOT follow: the Description of ContactStatus still cites Entities.ContactStatus.Open after Open is repointed and deleted - author text, corrected by hand at the end.

ops._why: (0) BEFORE: the starting point is INHERITED - Records 3, Attributes 3 and the Description that the other job wrote, citing Entities.ContactStatus.Open. Keep the ObjectKey: the get (7b) has to bring the same one with Records 2, and the get (11a) the same one again after the copy has gone away.
(1) BEFORE, the default-consumer: DefaultValue 'Entities.ContactStatus.Open'. No op of this job writes this text.

(2) BEFORE, who holds Open: count 2, real 2 - the filter (IServerAction:Contact_CountActive/IAggregateNode:GetActive/DataTable/ICombineSourcesOperation:Contacts/IFilter/IExpression) and the default (IServerEntity:Contact/IEntityAttribute:StatusId/IExpression). These are the two keys that (5b) has to return on Pending.
(3) BEFORE, the record that is going to receive the consumers: count 0, real 0. It was born in the other job and nobody cites it yet.

(4) CHANGE 1 - repoint EVERY consumer of Open to Pending: two IRecords of the same entity, the same interface, without force. It is the Studio's AbstractObject.ReplaceReferences and not a text search-and-replace: it returns consumers 2, rewired 2, stillPointingAtFrom 0, consumersOfTo 2, scope direct-external-nonderived, and the list touched with the two expressions. The consumer keys do not change - only the object they point to.
(5a) AFTER: DefaultValue 'Entities.ContactStatus.Pending' - the platform regenerated the text from the new binding. Compare with the get (1).

(5b) the filter too: the Condition of the IFilter says 'Contact.StatusId = Entities.ContactStatus.Pending'. It is the same IFilter (same key) as in the dumps of the other job - fourth rewrite of the same expression without an author touching it.
(5c) count 0, real 0: Open was left with nobody. It is this read that opens the door to the delete without force.

(5d) count 2, real 2: the SAME two consumers of the usages (2), with the same keys and the text already saying Pending. Compare with (3): from 0 to 2, and what changed was not the record, it was who cites it.

(6) CHANGE 2 - delete the record that was left without consumers. WITHOUT force: it is the replace that makes this possible. It returns brokenConsumers 0. Before the replace the same op is refused naming the two consumers (tests/jobs-negative/delete-static-record-in-use.json).

(7a) AFTER: Records 2 (it was 3 in the get (0)), Attributes 3, the same ObjectKey. And the Description STILL citing Entities.ContactStatus.Open - a record that no longer exists. Author text does not follow replace or delete; it is left for (12a).

ops.name: Open
ops._why: (7b) EMPTY list: nothing in the module answers to Open. The record really went away, it was not just hidden.

(8) CHANGE 3 - the Studio's Ctrl+D on the inherited entity: the copy goes into the SAME parent (Headless_CS) and the name is chosen by the PLATFORM - ContactStatus2. The alias $copy exists because THIS job created it; the original is still cited by path.

(9a) the copy: Name ContactStatus2, Label 'Contact Status 2', LabelPlural 'Contact Status 2s' (derived from the new name), Records 2 and Attributes 3 like the original, and the Description COPIED word by word - with the dead citation and everything. New ObjectKey, of course.

(9b) the tree of the copy: 3 IEntityAttribute with new keys, 2 IRecord (Pending and Closed) with the 3 IRecordAttributeValue and the values copied ("Pending"/3, "Closed"/2), and its OWN GetContactStatus2 and 'ContactStatus2 Identifier' - the copy of an entity brings its entity actions and its identifier.

(9c) count 1, real 1, and the only consumer is the IAttribute ContactStatus2 of the 'ContactStatus2 Record' (IAnonymousStructure:ContactStatus2 Record/IAttribute:ContactStatus2) - generated by the PLATFORM with the entity, written by no author. No expression cites the copy: whoever used the original keeps using the original.
(9d) the original lost nobody: count 3, real 3 - the two expressions (now citing Pending) and the IAttribute of the 'ContactStatus Record'. Duplicating does not split consumers.

ops.name: ContactStatus2
ops._why: (9e) two objects answer to the name of the copy: the IStaticEntity and the IAttribute of the anonymous record. Keep the list: the find (10b) shows which of the two survives the delete.

(10a) CHANGE 4 - delete the copy. The ONLY force of this job, and only because the delete without force was REFUSED by a consumer that the platform generated by itself, measured: "delete: refused, IStaticEntity 'ContactStatus2' is used by 1 consumer(s): IAnonymousStructure:ContactStatus2 Record/IAttribute:ContactStatus2 (list them with usages, fix or remove those usages, or pass \"force\": true to break them)". There are no author usages to fix (the (9c) showed it), and the anonymous record cannot be deleted by any op - so the force breaks exactly that consumer and no other: brokenConsumers 1.

ops.name: ContactStatus2
ops._why: (10b) AFTER: the IStaticEntity disappeared, but the IAttribute ContactStatus2 of the anonymous record is STILL in the list - it is the broken consumer of (10a), left behind in the module. The Verify stays clean (no new message), but it is a leftover that the Studio, when deleting through the interface, would not leave; whoever deletes a duplicated entity through this verb gets to know that its 'X Record' survives.

(10c) the leftover seen up close, resolved by type:name in the whole module: an OutSystems.Model.Types.IAttribute with WasDeleted False and IsValid True - it is not a ghost of the find list, it is really alive, inside the IAnonymousStructure 'ContactStatus2 Record' (ParentStructure). Note the DataType and the Type at null: the type of this attribute WAS the deleted entity, and that is what the force broke. It is the only vestige of the copy and it triggers no message in the Verify.
(11a) WHAT REMAINED: the original, with the same ObjectKey as the get (0), Records 2, Attributes 3. Deleting the copy did not touch the original.
(11b) and the two consumers are still on Pending, with the same keys as the (5d). Duplicating and deleting the copy did not touch whoever uses the original.

ops.value: Estado de um contacto. O valor por omissao de Contact.StatusId e Entities.ContactStatus.Pending; o registo Open foi repontado para Pending e apagado por static-record-refactor.json.
ops._why: (12a) the manual correction of what the (7a) showed does not follow: the Description is author text and still cited the deleted Open. Written at the end, after all the changes, so that the data contract reads it back as it is.

(12b) the final tree: the 3 attributes, the 2 records that remained (Closed and Pending, with the values intact), the GetContactStatus and the 'ContactStatus Identifier'. Without Open, without the copy, and without a single expression rewritten by an author: the replace did the work and the delete only passed because it came first.
